domain_label: Turlock Ag & Specialty — Market, Demand & Saturation Economics
purpose: A method for sizing and reading the Turlock independent Ag & Specialty market, a sector split into two economies sharing one label: a B2B ag spine (Ag Equipment & Repair, Feed/Farm Supply, Large-Animal/Dairy Vet) whose demand unit is the county dairy herd and planted acreage rather than residents, and a thin-demand discretionary consumer edge (Bike Shop, Music/Instruments, Cottage-Food/Farm Stand) whose demand is resident- and student-driven and leakage-prone. The method quantifies each economy's correct demand base, explains why this many operators saturate at the count they do, separates the B2B white-space from the crowded consumer lines, accounts for herd/harvest seasonality, locates licensing-and-labor-gated openings, and expresses every revenue, margin and market-size figure strictly as a labeled benchmark estimate (industry benchmark x observable size signal) rather than as a stated fact for any named business.
assumptions: no per-business revenue dataset is supplied; every dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual reported figure for any named business
the universe is the 14 verified Turlock Ag & Specialty independents in businesses.json (chains excluded), as of the 2026-06-30 snapshot, reported as a coverage floor not a ceiling
city/county/state figures (population, county ag value, dairy count, CSLB/CFO fees, statutory caps) are cited public facts or explicitly labeled derivations

sub-category revenue bands are published industry benchmarks (per veterinarian, per farm-supply store, per shop) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal (firm age, division count, format), tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
the B2B half is a derivative bet on Stanislaus County dairy and almond cash flow, so its true demand unit is herd count and planted acreage, not city headcount
Modesto (~218k, ~20 minutes north) plus national e-commerce (Amazon, Chewy, Tractor Supply.com, Sweetwater) are the leakage anchors capping the consumer lines

the single highest-leverage confirmation for the uncertain dollar figures is the annual Stanislaus County Crop Report (herd/acre/value) paired with CDTFA sales-tax receipts and DVM-count-per-practice disclosure
exclusions: per-sub-category sourcing, OEM dealer affiliations, cold-chain and fleet operations detail — covered by the supply-chain KB
per-sub-category cost-structure and go/no-go business-model detail beyond the revenue/margin pairing — covered by the business-models KB
any claim of an actual, reported, or audited dollar revenue, DVM count, or headcount for a named business
chain and franchise operators (Tractor Supply, big-box), which are outside the independents-only catalog
individual pricing, marketing, or service-bundling tactics for a specific operator

competency_questions.question: Why is the Ag & Specialty label really two economies, and what distinct demand base does each half answer to?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TWO_ECONOMIES_SPLIT names Economy A (B2B ag spine: equipment, feed, vet — non-discretionary, herd/acre-scaled) and Economy B (discretionary consumer edge: bike, music, cottage-food) and states each half's correct demand unit

competency_questions.question: How does the county dairy/almond base act as the expander that lifts the B2B count above a generic same-size town?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DAIRY_ALMOND_BASE ties the ~$3.15B ag value and ~132 dairies to why a 73k town carries three vets, three equipment firms and three feed outlets, as cited public facts

competency_questions.question: Why is the herd/acre base, not city residents, the correct demand denominator for the B2B lines, and what does the per-practice herd ratio show?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HERD_DENOMINATOR shows per-resident framing is meaningless for B2B and gives the ~44-dairies-per-vet-practice labeled derivation against the ~132-dairy base

competency_questions.question: What sizes the thin consumer-edge demand, and why is it the most leakage-prone half?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMER_DEMAND_EDGE quantifies the ~72,919 resident + ~8,455-student base and the school-band/CSU recurring channels, and flags Modesto/online leakage as the structural cap

competency_questions.question: How is a per-sub-category benchmark revenue band built so it is an honest estimate and never a stated fact for a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_BANDS states the benchmark x size-signal method, gives the per-sub-category bands, and tags every band estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: Why is high gross in a sub-category not high net, and how is each band paired with its cost/margin reality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_MARGIN_PAIRING pairs each band with its COGS/labor/net reality (feed ~70-80% COGS ~2-6% net; vet high labor ~35-50%, ~10-18% net) so a high-gross band is never read as high-profit

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain roughly 14 Ag & Specialty independents — not 6, not 30 — and what three gates set that equilibrium?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_EQUILIBRIUM names the three-gate filter (dairy/almond base as expander, statute+scarce labor as the B2B cap, demand thinness+leakage as the consumer cap) and ties the ~14 count to it

competency_questions.question: Which sub-categories are saturated, white-space-adjacent, or capped, read against the correct denominator?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PER_SUBCAT_SATURATION gives a per-sub-category count, per-10k or per-herd read, and a saturated / white-space / capped verdict for each of the six sub-categories

competency_questions.question: Why is the competitive map the inverse of a normal retail town, with consumer lines crowded and B2B lines white-space-adjacent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITIVE_STRUCTURE explains why music is internally crowded, vets contest herd accounts, and feed/equipment are under-stored against the county base

competency_questions.question: What licensing and scarce-labor gates cap the B2B lines so the count cannot simply expand to meet demand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSING_LABOR_GATE names the CSLB C-57/C-61 trades, vet board/DEA/mobility-act gates, the ~1.3%-food-animal-vet labor scarcity, and the wholesale/capital barrier as the binding B2B caps

competency_questions.question: How does where demand leaks out of Turlock cap the consumer lines, and what is the leakage rule?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODESTO_ONLINE_LEAKAGE states the Modesto + online anchors and the rule that the shippable/price-comparable/non-urgent dollar leaks while the urgent/fitted/serviced/herd-side dollar stays local

competency_questions.question: Where is the defensible white-space once both demand and the licensing/labor/capital gate are considered, and how is a market go/no-go reached and refreshed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WHITESPACE_GATED ranks the gated openings and MARKET_GO_NOGO composes the saturation read, white-space rank, and the cost gate into a verdict refusing demand-true but gate-locked additions, while MARKET_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh cadence and triggers (new crop report, herd shock, fee change) that re-run the reads

glossary.definition: The defining structural fact that Ag & Specialty is not one sector but two sharing a label: Economy A, a non-discretionary B2B ag spine (equipment, feed, vet) scaled to the county herd and acreage; and Economy B, a discretionary consumer edge (bike, music, cottage-food) scaled to residents and students and leakage-prone.

The principle that the correct demand unit for the B2B lines is the county dairy herd (~132 commercial dairies) and planted acreage, not city residents; a per-resident saturation read for a large-animal vet or feed outlet is meaningless and understates the demand base.

The honest revenue-estimation method used throughout: take a published per-veterinarian / per-store / per-shop industry benchmark and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (firm age, division count, multi-vet vs single, format), yielding a band tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level.

The discipline of pairing every revenue band with its cost/margin reality so a high top-line is never read as high profit; feed runs ~70-80% COGS and ~2-6% net, and vet practices carry ~35-50% labor and only ~10-18% net despite large gross.

The explanation of why the count is ~14: the dairy/almond base is the expander lifting it above a generic town, statute plus scarce specialized labor cap the B2B lines, and demand thinness plus leakage cap the consumer lines; the count is herd-pulled up and gate-pinned in place.

The rule governing the consumer edge: the shippable, price-comparable, non-urgent dollar leaks out to Modesto big-box and online (Amazon, Chewy, Sweetwater, Tractor Supply.com), while the urgent, fitted, serviced, or herd-side dollar stays local — every durable independent sells service-proximity the internet cannot ship.

The finding that Feed/Farm Supply and Ag Equipment & Repair are under-stored against the ~132-dairy base, not over-built; the binding entry constraint is wholesale/distributor access, capital, and CSLB-licensed scarce trades, not a shortage of customers.

The binding cap on the vet line: only ~1.3% of US vets do food-animal work and rural vets average ~52 hr/week, so the constraint on new practices is trained food-animal people, not license availability or customers.

The convention that the count of 14 is the verified minimum of independent Ag & Specialty operators found via public sources, not a claim of completeness; additional micro-producers and small feed/tack shops plausibly exist below the visibility threshold and would only raise the count.

The dominant sector risk that vet, equipment and feed demand all derive from the same dairy/almond cash flow, so a milk-price downturn or herd shock (e.g., the 2024 avian-flu quarantine of >110 of 132 dairies) compresses four of six sub-categories at once rather than being offset across them.

source_registry.description: labeled benchmark estimates and cited public facts for the Turlock independent Ag & Specialty market, grounded in the ag_specialty deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its upstream supply_ops.md / market_saturation.md / reconciled.md briefs, and the 14-business source dataset (businesses.json); demand sizing for the B2B spine uses the county dairy count and ag value rather than population, consumer-edge sizing uses resident and CSU figures, sub-category revenue bands use published vet/farm-supply/music/bike/CFO benchmarks, and saturation reads use per-10k density against the correct demand denominator
source_registry.citation_or_locator: 2024 Stanislaus County Agricultural Report (~$3.15B gross ag value, ~132 commercial dairies, ~6% 2024 value decline, >110/132 avian-flu quarantine); Census QuickFacts (Turlock ~72,919 pop, $82,995 median HH income, 46.1% Hispanic); CSU Stanislaus enrollment (~8,455 students Fall 2024); AVMA / iVET360 2024 (per-veterinarian benchmark, ~1.3% food-animal vets, ~52 hr/week); IBISWorld Farm Supply Stores 2025 (~19,485 US stores); NBDA / Bicycle Retailer (US bike-shop count 6,195->3,600 2000-2022); MusicShop360 2024-25; CSLB (C-57, C-61/D-21); CA Cottage Food Law / CDPH (2025 caps ~$86,206 Class A / ~$172,411 Class B); ag_specialty DEEPDIVE.md, supply_ops.md, market_saturation.md, reconciled.md, businesses.json

nodes.definition: Establish the sector's defining structural fact: Ag & Specialty is not one market but two that share a label. Economy A is the B2B ag spine — Ag Equipment & Repair (Sallaberry, TDR, Dairy Solutions Group), Feed/Farm Supply (Stanislaus Farm Supply, Turlock Feed, Elite) and Large-Animal/Dairy Vet (Azores, Lander, Mid Valley) — selling to commercial operators, with non-discretionary, herd/acre-scaled, cash/net-terms demand and no insurance buffer. Economy B is the discretionary consumer edge — Bike Shop (Cycle Masters), Music/Instruments (Hendrickson's, Dale's, Ingram's) and the Cottage-Food/Farm Stand (Cipponeri) — selling to households, with episodic, leakage-prone demand. Every demand, saturation and revenue read in this KB must first place a business in the correct economy because the two answer to different denominators.

included: the Economy A B2B spine and its three sub-categories
the Economy B consumer edge and its three sub-categories
excluded: the dollar size of either economy
the herd-vs-resident denominator mechanics (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a business's economy/sub-category classification changes

pros.claim: Splitting the sector into two economies prevents reading a herd-scaled vet by the same denominator as a household bike shop
pros.example: three large-animal vets look over-built per resident but are matched to herd load once placed in Economy A

cons.claim: Two straddling businesses blur the split, so the clean six-way grouping is fuzzier at the edges
cons.example: Stanislaus Farm Supply carries an Ag Equipment secondary and Turlock Feed an Apparel secondary, crossing the line

failure_modes: reading a B2B sub-category by a per-resident denominator
treating the discretionary consumer edge as non-discretionary like the ag spine
acceptance_tests: both economies are named with their three sub-categories each, and each economy's demand character (non-discretionary herd/acre-scaled vs discretionary resident-scaled) is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: a business changes primary category or enters/exits the catalog
a straddle reclassification shifts a sub-category between economies

nodes.definition: Name the single dominant economic fact that expands the B2B count above a generic same-size town: Turlock sits inside Stanislaus County, whose 2024 gross agricultural value was ~$3.15B [FACT, 2024 Crop Report], led by almonds (~$825M) and milk (~$755M) and anchored by a cluster of ~132 commercial dairies [FACT]. This concentrated dairy/almond base is the only reason a 73k town carries three large-animal vets, three ag-equipment firms and three feed outlets at all; a generic town with no dairy cluster would carry a fraction of these. Almond hulls feed dairy cattle, integrating the two crops, so the equipment, feed and vet lines are all derivative bets on the same dairy/almond cash flow — the source of both the count and its principal forward risk.

included: the ~$3.15B ag value and ~132-dairy cluster as the expander
the crop integration via almond hulls
excluded: the per-practice herd ratio (its own node)
the labor/statute caps on the count

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a county ag value, dairy count, or crop figure is refreshed

pros.claim: Anchoring the count to a cited county ag base explains a B2B density national models under-predict
pros.example: three of each B2B format is rational only against a ~132-dairy, ~$3.15B base, not against 73k residents

cons.claim: Concentrating demand in one base means the whole B2B half rises and falls with dairy/almond cash flow together
cons.example: the 2024 ~6% county ag-value decline pressures vet, feed and equipment demand simultaneously

failure_modes: restating a year-stamped figure (e.g., 2020 almond acreage) as current
treating the ag base as a stable backdrop rather than the sector's chief correlated risk
acceptance_tests: the ~$3.15B ag value, the ~132-dairy cluster and the almond/milk lead are each stated as cited public facts and tied to why the B2B count is as high as it is
revisit_triggers: a new annual Stanislaus County Crop Report lands
a milk-price or herd shock changes the ag base
an almond-acreage refresh updates the planted-acre figure

nodes.definition: Size the demand base for Economy B, the discretionary consumer edge, which answers to residents and students rather than the herd. Turlock is a town of ~72,919 residents (July 2025) [FACT, Census] with median household income ~$82,995 [FACT] and ~8,455 CSU Stanislaus students (Fall 2024) [FACT]. For the consumer edge the two structural demand drivers are the university and the K-12 school-band pipeline: Hendrickson's owns the school band/orchestra + piano channel, Dale's the lesson/repair recurring model, Ingram's the rental-fleet model, while Cycle Masters and Cipponeri sell to general households. This demand is discretionary, episodic and the most leakage-prone half of the sector, surviving on service, recurring relationships and local captivity rather than price-comparable boxed-goods sales.

included: resident base, income and CSU enrollment
the school-band and university demand drivers
excluded: the leakage mechanism detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a resident, income, or enrollment figure changes

pros.claim: Naming the school-band and CSU channels explains why three music stores survive in a 73k town
pros.example: the three coexist only because each owns a defensible recurring channel rather than competing on new-gear retail

cons.claim: Discretionary resident demand is thin and a single bad year can erode the fragile consumer edge
cons.example: a nationally contracting bike category leaves Cycle Masters at a one-store equilibrium with no room for a second

failure_modes: treating CSU enrollment as net-new spend rather than partly overlapping resident demand
reading the consumer edge as price-competitive retail when it survives on service and recurring channels
acceptance_tests: the ~72,919 resident base and ~8,455-student figure are stated as public facts and each consumer sub-category is tied to its demand driver and recurring channel
revisit_triggers: a census/ACS demographic refresh
a CSU enrollment release
a school-music-program funding change shifts the band pipeline

nodes.definition: Establish that the correct demand denominator for the B2B lines is the county herd and planted acreage, not city residents, and that a per-resident saturation read is meaningless for them. Read against the wrong denominator, three feed outlets is 0.41 per 10k city residents; read against the right one, ~19,485 US farm-supply stores imply ~0.57 per 10k nationally, so three outlets against ~132 dairies plus thousands of acres is thin, not crowded. For vets, the working ratio is ~132 dairies / 3 = ~44 dairies per practice [ESTIMATE, derived] plus beef, swine and small-ruminant load — a matched ratio, not oversupply. Every B2B saturation read in this KB must use the herd/acre denominator and flag the per-resident framing as inapplicable.

excluded: the per-sub-category saturation verdicts (their own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the dairy count, acre base, or B2B operator count changes

pros.claim: Using the herd denominator corrects a per-resident read that would falsely call the B2B lines over-built
pros.example: three feed outlets read crowded per resident but under-stored against ~132 dairies and thousands of acres

cons.claim: The ~44-dairies-per-practice ratio is a derived estimate that ignores beef/swine/small-ruminant load and per-dairy size variance
cons.example: a few very large dairies could shift the effective ratio well off the simple 132/3 division

failure_modes: applying a per-10k resident benchmark to a herd-scaled B2B line
treating the ~44-dairies-per-vet figure as a measured fact rather than a labeled derivation
acceptance_tests: the herd/acre denominator is named as correct for the B2B lines, the ~44-dairies-per-vet-practice ratio is given as a labeled derivation, and the per-resident framing is flagged inapplicable
revisit_triggers: the county dairy count changes in a new crop report
a B2B operator enters or exits
a planted-acre refresh changes the acre base

nodes.definition: Build the per-sub-category revenue bands that are the primary, most defensible revenue view, every one a labeled estimate (published benchmark x observable Turlock size signal), never an actual figure for a named business. Representative bands per single operator: Large-Animal/Dairy Vet ~$0.75M-$3M (per-veterinarian benchmark ~$250k-$375k x est. 2-6 DVMs, multi-vet/lab divisions an upside signal); Ag Equipment & Repair ~$0.5M-$5M+ (small pump shop low end, full dairy design/construction like TDR high end); Feed/Farm Supply ~$0.5M-$3M (US farm-supply band on bulk-volume low margin); Music/Instruments ~$0.25M-$0.75M (small-shop band with rentals+lessons+repair stabilizing); Bike Shop ~$0.3M-$0.8M (single-store NBDA norm, contracting category caps upside); Cottage-Food/Farm Stand <$50k-$150k (CFO ceiling on the processed slice plus seasonal stand throughput). Each band is tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence and a confirmation path.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark source or measured size signal changes

pros.claim: Per-sub-category bands anchored to published benchmarks give a planning estimate without quoting any operator
pros.example: a vet band of ~$0.75M-$3M from a per-DVM benchmark x estimated DVM count is auditable and business-agnostic

cons.claim: Bands rest on national benchmarks and unobserved size signals, so any single business can sit far outside its band
cons.example: the equipment band ~$0.5M-$5M+ is the widest and lowest-confidence because a parlor build dwarfs a pump repair

failure_modes: attaching a band to a named business as if it were that business's revenue
stating the vet band without flagging the unknown DVM-count-per-practice it hinges on
acceptance_tests: each of the six sub-categories has a band derived as benchmark x a stated size signal, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence and a confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark source updates (AVMA, IBISWorld, NBDA)
an observable size signal (DVM count, format) is measured for a sub-category
CDTFA distribution data lands

nodes.definition: Pair each revenue band with its cost/margin reality so a high gross is never read as high net — the discipline that high revenue is not high profit. Labeled estimates: Feed/Farm Supply runs ~70-80% COGS (commodity feed is low-margin) and only ~2-6% net, lifted only by cooperative scale (Stanislaus FS via Valley Wide) or blended service margin (Turlock Feed's sharpening/tack); Large-Animal/Dairy Vet carries high labor ~35-50% (licensed DVMs are the scarce, expensive, binding input) and ~10-18% net despite large gross; Ag Equipment ~40-55% parts COGS on service with ~8-15% net swung widely by project mix; Music ~40-60% on instrument resale but far lower on lessons/repair, ~5-12% net; Bike ~50-60% goods, ~5-10% net with service the margin saver. Every band node in this KB inherits this pairing.

included: the survival levers that lift thin margins

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cost benchmark or margin lever changes

pros.claim: Pairing each band with its margin reality stops a high top-line being mistaken for high profit
pros.example: feed's ~$0.5M-$3M band is a ~2-6% net business, not a high-profit one, once COGS is shown

cons.claim: Margin estimates are sector-typical ranges, not the actual books of any named business, so they too are uncertain
cons.example: coop scale could push Stanislaus FS net above the small-store band the estimate assumes

failure_modes: dropping the cost/margin pairing so a high-gross sub-category reads as high-profit
applying a single net margin across the whole sector despite wide cross-line variance
acceptance_tests: each major sub-category's band is paired with a labeled COGS/labor/net estimate and the high-gross-not-high-net rule is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: a cost benchmark (wages, feed commodity price) updates
a coop-pricing or service-mix change shifts a line's margin
actual margin data becomes available to replace an estimate

nodes.definition: Correct the common misread of treating a sub-category band as a point figure or applying the wrong band to a named operator. The Ag Equipment & Repair band ~$0.5M-$5M+ is the widest and lowest-confidence in the set because project mix swings it enormously — a full dairy parlor build (TDR-type, founded 1972) dwarfs a single pump repair (a Sallaberry-type job), so no single midpoint describes the line. The vet band hinges on an unknown DVM count per practice, the most load-bearing unknown in the sizing. The primary read is always the labeled band with its confidence, never a point estimate; the single best resolution is operator-level disclosure (DVM count, project mix) or CDTFA distribution, not a tighter guess.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: operator-level size signal or distribution data appears

pros.claim: Flagging band-not-point stops a reader collapsing a ~$0.5M-$5M+ range into a single misleading midpoint
pros.example: averaging the equipment band hides that a parlor build and a pump repair are orders of magnitude apart

cons.claim: Insisting on wide bands limits how precisely downstream planning can use the revenue view
cons.example: a ~$0.5M-$5M+ equipment band is too wide to set a precise entry target on

failure_modes: quoting a band midpoint as a typical operator's revenue
ignoring that the vet band's accuracy is gated by the unknown DVM count
acceptance_tests: the equipment band is labeled the widest/lowest-confidence with its project-mix cause, and the DVM-count-per-practice is named as the load-bearing unknown behind the vet band
revisit_triggers: operator-level project mix or DVM count is disclosed
the benchmark bands are revised
CDTFA outlet-level distribution appears

nodes.definition: Explain why Turlock sustains roughly 14 Ag & Specialty independents — not 6, not 30 — via a three-gate filter in order of bindingness. Gate one, the expander: the dairy/almond base (~132 dairies, ~$3.15B) lifts the B2B count above a generic town, so three of each B2B format exist at all. Gate two, the B2B cap: statute (CSLB, vet board) plus scarce specialized labor (~1.3% of US vets do food-animal work) and wholesale/capital access cap the B2B lines from going higher. Gate three, the consumer cap: demand thinness plus Modesto/online leakage hold bike at a one-store equilibrium and make three music stores viable only via captive recurring channels. The count is herd-pulled up and gate-pinned in place; the binding constraints are licensing, scarce labor and leakage — not lack of customers.

included: the three-gate filter and its ordering
excluded: the licensing/labor gate detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: one of the three equilibrium gates shifts

pros.claim: Framing 14 as a three-gate equilibrium resists both an over-build and an under-build read of the count
pros.example: it explains why the B2B lines have headroom yet the count is still capped by labor and statute

cons.claim: An equilibrium framing can imply false stability when the dairy base and bike category are moving
cons.example: a herd-count collapse or further bike-category contraction would shift the equilibrium the framing holds fixed

failure_modes: reading the count as a customer-demand deficit and recommending broad expansion
ignoring that the equilibrium drifts as the ag base, statute or leakage change
acceptance_tests: all three gates are named in order (base expander, B2B statute/labor cap, consumer thinness/leakage cap) and tied to the ~14-count outcome with the count flagged as not customer-limited
revisit_triggers: one of the three gates shifts (ag base, B2B labor/statute, consumer leakage)
the independent count moves away from ~14

nodes.definition: Give the per-sub-category saturation read by setting each catalog count against the correct denominator. Bike Shop 1 (0.14/10k vs US ~0.11/10k) at-market and at a one-store equilibrium in a contracting category. Music/Instruments 3 (0.41/10k) over-indexed vs population but justified by school-band + CSU recurring revenue, genuinely crowded for 73k. Feed/Farm Supply 3 read against ~132 dairies + acres is under-saturated, not crowded. Ag Equipment & Repair 3 is white-space-adjacent, county-scaled to capital-equipment cycles. Large-Animal/Dairy Vet 3 at ~44 dairies/practice is tightly matched to the herd base, not oversupply. Cottage-Food/Farm Stand 1 is structurally capped by CFO statute on its processed slice, not demand-capped. Two straddles (Stanislaus FS, Turlock Feed) make the clean 3/3/3/3/1/1 split fuzzier at the edges.

included: per-sub-category count, density read and saturated/white-space/capped verdict
excluded: the white-space ranking and cost gate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sub-category count or its denominator changes

pros.claim: A count-vs-correct-denominator table makes each sub-category's saturation legible at a glance
pros.example: feed 3 reads under-saturated against dairies while music 3 reads crowded against residents

cons.claim: Denominators and ceilings are themselves estimates, so a saturated/white-space read can flip if mis-set
cons.example: the vet 'matched' read reverses if the effective herd-per-practice load is higher than the simple ratio

failure_modes: reading a primary-category count as the full picture when secondary straddles shift it
applying a per-resident density to a B2B line and calling it crowded
acceptance_tests: each of the six sub-categories has a catalog count, the correct denominator/density read, and a saturated / white-space-adjacent / capped verdict consistent with the three gates
revisit_triggers: a sub-category opens or closes in the catalog
the dairy count or resident base shifts a denominator
a straddle reclassification changes a count

nodes.definition: Model where demand leaks out of Turlock and why it caps the consumer lines. Local/regional leakage runs to Modesto (~218k, ~20 minutes north) big-box and dealer networks, and to Tractor Supply / Rural King-style chains on commodity feed-and-supply. National/online leakage runs to Amazon, Chewy and Tractor Supply.com (feed/supply), Sweetwater, Guitar Center and Amazon (instruments), and direct-to-consumer plus Amazon (bikes/parts). The leakage rule: the shippable, price-comparable, non-urgent dollar leaks out; the urgent, fitted, serviced, or herd-side dollar stays local. This rule is why the consumer edge survives only on service-proximity the internet cannot ship, and why a nationally contracting bike category holds Cycle Masters at a one-store equilibrium.

excluded: the licensing/labor gate on the B2B lines

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: leakage behavior or a national consumer category shifts

pros.claim: The leakage rule explains the consumer one-store equilibrium that demand math alone cannot
pros.example: a second bike shop would split a thin, leakage-prone household demand already going to Amazon and Modesto

cons.claim: Leakage is inferred from proximity and category, not measured, so its magnitude is uncertain
cons.example: without a cross-shop study the exact share of Turlock bike/instrument spend going to Modesto/online is unknown

failure_modes: treating the leakage estimate as a measured figure
applying the leakage rule to herd-side B2B demand that does not leak (urgent, on-call, near the herd)
acceptance_tests: the Modesto and online leakage anchors are named and the leakage rule (shippable/price-comparable/non-urgent leaks; urgent/fitted/serviced/herd-side stays) is stated explicitly as an estimate of behavior
revisit_triggers: a Modesto/online cross-shop study quantifies the leakage
a national category (e.g., bike) contracts or recovers
a new big-box or chain opens nearby

nodes.definition: Read the sector's competitive map as the inverse of a normal retail town: the consumer lines are crowded and the B2B lines are white-space-adjacent. Music/Instruments is the most internally competitive consumer line — three stores coexist only because each owns a defensible recurring channel (Hendrickson's school-band+piano, Dale's lessons/repair, Ingram's rental/repair logistics); it is crowded and surviving, the most demand-fragile line. Large-Animal/Dairy Vet is competitive among the three but contests herd accounts and 24/7-coverage reputation against a shared ~132-dairy base large enough to sustain all three absent a herd collapse. Feed/Farm Supply and Ag Equipment are not over-stored against the county base; the entry constraint is buying-power parity and CSLB-licensed trades, not too many sellers. Bike sits at a one-store equilibrium and Cottage-Food is white-space by count but capped by law.

excluded: the licensing/labor gate detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sub-category's competitor set or recurring channel changes

pros.claim: The inverse-map framing explains why the consumer lines are crowded while the B2B lines have headroom
pros.example: three music stores are genuinely crowded for 73k while three feed outlets are thin against ~132 dairies

cons.claim: The map can imply B2B entry is easy when the gate, not competition, is the real barrier
cons.example: feed has demand headroom but a new entrant still cannot match coop buying power without scale

failure_modes: mistaking B2B white-space for easy entry when licensing/capital gate it
treating the crowded music line as price-competitive when each survives on a separate recurring channel
acceptance_tests: the consumer lines are read as crowded (music) or one-store (bike) and the B2B lines as white-space-adjacent against the county base, with each music store's distinct recurring channel named
revisit_triggers: a competitor enters or exits a sub-category
a recurring channel (school band, herd account) shifts
the dairy base changes the vet contest

nodes.definition: Define the entry gate that caps the B2B lines so the count cannot expand to meet demand — the barrier the saturation view alone misses. Pump/well and dairy construction (Sallaberry, TDR) require CSLB C-57 Well Drilling, commonly paired with C-61/D-21 Machinery & Pumps, plus contractor bond and commercial fleet insurance. Veterinary (Azores, Lander, Mid Valley) requires CA Veterinary Medical Board premises registration, DVM/RVT licensure, VACSP permits, and per-premises DEA registration with the Veterinary Medicine Mobility Act allowing field-carried controlled substances. The truly binding shortage is trained food-animal labor — only ~1.3% of US vets do food-animal work, rural vets average ~52 hr/week, and skilled trades (pump techs, welders, electricians) are scarce in a tight rural pool. Feed faces wholesale-distributor access and capital (why Stanislaus FS joined Valley Wide). New B2B entrants compete for licensed people and capital, not customers.

included: CSLB, vet board, DEA and mobility-act gates

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a licensing rule, labor-supply figure, or wholesale barrier changes

pros.claim: Foregrounding the licensing/labor gate explains why demand-open B2B lines still cannot simply expand
pros.example: a new vet practice cannot be willed into existence because trained food-animal DVMs do not exist to staff it

cons.claim: Gate detail varies by line and the binding constraint differs, so a single barrier figure oversimplifies
cons.example: the gate is labor for vets, capital/wholesale for feed, and CSLB trades for equipment — not one wall

failure_modes: treating B2B white-space as enterable on demand alone without the licensing/labor gate
conflating DVM license availability with the deeper trained-food-animal-labor scarcity
acceptance_tests: the CSLB, vet-board/DEA, and wholesale/capital gates are each named per B2B line and the ~1.3%-food-animal-vet labor scarcity is stated as the binding cap, with people/capital not customers identified as the constraint
revisit_triggers: a CSLB or vet-board licensing rule changes
a food-animal vet labor-supply figure updates
a wholesale/cooperative access shift changes the feed barrier

nodes.definition: State the premise the licensing/labor gate rests on: the B2B lines are demand-open but gate-locked, the mirror image of the consumer lines being gate-open but demand-locked. Feed and equipment have genuine demand headroom against the ~132-dairy, multi-thousand-acre base, and the vets are matched to herd load, so customers are not the constraint on any B2B line. What stops the count rising is upstream — licensed/trained people, regulatory premises gates, and wholesale-supply/capital access. This premise separates the B2B half cleanly from the consumer half so the gate node can attach the specific statutory and labor barriers to a demand-open, not demand-saturated, baseline.

included: the mirror with gate-open-but-demand-locked consumer lines
excluded: the specific CSLB/vet/feed gates (their own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: B2B demand headroom against the herd base changes

pros.claim: Naming the demand-open baseline prevents reading a B2B cap as a demand deficit
pros.example: feed headroom against the herd base shows the cap is upstream, not a shortage of customers

cons.claim: The premise treats demand as open uniformly when sub-lines differ in headroom
cons.example: equipment capital-project demand is lumpier than continuous feed demand, so 'open' varies by line

failure_modes: reading B2B demand-open as B2B easy-entry
applying the demand-open premise to the demand-locked consumer lines
acceptance_tests: the B2B lines are stated as demand-open but gate-locked, mirrored against the consumer lines as gate-open but demand-locked, with customers named as not the binding B2B constraint
revisit_triggers: the herd/acre base changes B2B demand headroom
a B2B line shifts from demand-open to demand-saturated

nodes.definition: Overlay the agricultural calendar — planting, almond harvest, calving/repro, irrigation load — onto each line so the demand peaks a flat annual band hides surface as a working-capital risk. Feed/Farm Supply peaks at spring planting (seed, fertilizer, crop-protection pre-book) and summer/fall almond season, with hay/forage swinging on dairy rations and water cost. Ag Equipment and Vets see repair pressure around calving/repro cycles and summer well/pump irrigation load, with vets carrying 24/7 emergency year-round. Music spikes back-to-school (Aug-Sep) on band rentals plus a holiday bump. Bike runs a spring/summer riding-season peak with a winter service lull. Cottage-Food (Cipponeri) has a sharp summer stone-fruit window with honey/dried fruit extending the shelf-stable shoulder. An operator reading only the annual band will mis-plan cash flow through the troughs.

included: music back-to-school, bike riding-season, cottage-food stone-fruit windows

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a seasonal peak's timing or magnitude is observed to change

pros.claim: Surfacing herd/harvest/academic peaks turns a flat annual band into an actionable cash-flow profile
pros.example: feed's spring pre-book and almond-season peak are its volume engine, invisible in an annual average

cons.claim: Seasonality is hard to size without operator data, so peaks are directional not quantified
cons.example: knowing music spikes at back-to-school does not say by how much without sales records

failure_modes: averaging a stone-fruit- or back-to-school-concentrated business into a flat band and mis-sizing working capital
ignoring that the bike winter lull compounds a thin annual base
acceptance_tests: each seasonal sub-category is tied to its specific peak (planting/almond, calving/irrigation, back-to-school, riding-season, stone-fruit) and the working-capital risk is named explicitly
revisit_triggers: a crop-cycle or water-cost shift changes a peak
operator sales data quantifies a peak's magnitude
an academic-calendar change shifts the band-rental spike

nodes.definition: Separate growing from declining sub-categories using national trends overlaid on local fit. Under pressure/declining: Bike Shop sits in a nationally contracting category (US bike-specific shops fell ~6,195->3,600, 2000-2022 [FACT]), so one shop is the equilibrium, not a deficit; legacy feed independents without cooperative scale face margin compression (~2-6% net) squeezed by both the coop and big-box chains. Stable/herd-derivative: the B2B spine (vet, equipment, feed) is durable but trajectory is a derivative bet on dairy/almond cash flow — the 2024 ~6% county ag-value decline and the 2024 avian-flu quarantine of >110 of 132 dairies (a 2024 condition, not restated as live 2026) show the downside. Constrained/flat: Cottage-Food is held small by CFO statute on its processed slice. The honest read is that no line is a clean national growth lane; durability comes from the herd base and recurring channels, not category tailwinds.

included: the herd-derivative B2B trajectory and its 2024 shocks
excluded: the white-space ranking and gate (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a national category release or a crop-report trajectory change

pros.claim: Overlaying national trajectory on local fit distinguishes a contracting line from a herd-durable one
pros.example: bike is contracting nationally while the vet line is durable on the herd base despite no category tailwind

cons.claim: Herd-derivative durability is only as stable as the dairy base, which is itself volatile
cons.example: the 2024 avian-flu quarantine shows the B2B trajectory can compress sharply on an upstream shock

failure_modes: restating the 2024 avian-flu quarantine as a live 2026 condition
treating the contracting bike category as a deficit rather than a one-store equilibrium
acceptance_tests: bike is named as a contracting category at one-store equilibrium, feed as margin-compressed, and the B2B spine as herd-derivative with the 2024 shocks cited and date-stamped, not restated as current
revisit_triggers: a new national category release (bike, farm-supply)
a new crop report changes the herd-derivative trajectory
a feed margin or coop-pricing shift

nodes.definition: Locate and rank the defensible white-space, marking each viable only after its licensing/labor/capital gate clears — the inverse of the consumer lines, which are gate-open but demand-locked. Ranked B2B openings (demand-open, gate-locked): (1) additional Feed/Farm Supply capacity against the ~132-dairy base, viable only with cooperative or wholesale buying-power parity, the hardest gate; (2) Ag Equipment & Repair niche depth (pump/well, dairy systems), viable only with CSLB C-57/C-61 trades that cannot be readily hired in a tight rural pool; (3) Large-Animal/Dairy Vet capacity, demand-matched to the herd but gate-locked by the ~1.3%-food-animal-vet labor scarcity — you compete for people, not customers. Consumer/cottage openings (gate-open, demand-locked): a second bike or music store fails the demand gate; cottage-food has count headroom but each producer is CFO revenue-ceilinged, so structure around honey/whole produce (outside CFO) for headroom.

excluded: the per-decision go/no-go verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a white-space opening is entered or its demand/gate changes

pros.claim: Ranking white-space by demand and gate together prevents recommending a demand-true but un-enterable B2B opening
pros.example: feed ranks as demand-open headroom but is gated first by buying-power parity, so it is not a clean yes

cons.claim: A ranked list can read as a recommendation when each opening still needs an operator's own feasibility check
cons.example: vet capacity ranks on demand yet its labor gate could sink any specific entrant who cannot hire a food-animal DVM

failure_modes: listing B2B white-space on demand alone without the licensing/labor/capital gate
treating a consumer opening as white-space when it fails the demand gate
acceptance_tests: the B2B openings are ranked each with a demand basis and an explicit gate qualifier (buying-power, CSLB trades, food-animal labor), and the consumer/cottage lines are marked gate-open but demand-locked or statute-capped
revisit_triggers: a white-space opening is entered locally
a herd/ag-base shift changes an opening's demand
a licensing fee, labor supply, or wholesale access changes the gate

nodes.definition: Bind every dollar figure in the herd-and-acreage sizing to a labeled-estimate discipline: per-business revenue is not public for these privately held Ag independents, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business. Every sub-category dollar band is a labeled benchmark estimate (published benchmark x observable size signal) tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path; every high-gross band is paired with its thin-net-margin caveat; city/county/state figures (population, ~$3.15B ag value, ~132 dairies, CFO caps) are cited public facts or labeled derivations; supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference unless a cited source states otherwise. Method, public source and confidence must travel with every number. This guardrail governs how all sizing and band nodes may be expressed.

included: the public-fact-vs-derivation distinction and method-source-confidence travel rule

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new dollar figure is introduced or an actual datum becomes available

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail keeps every downstream number honest and auditable
pros.example: tagging every sub-category band estimate-not-actual prevents any figure being read as a named business's audited revenue

cons.claim: Heavy labeling can make the analysis read as hedged and lower its perceived usefulness
cons.example: a reader wanting one revenue number is frustrated by a band tagged low-confidence

failure_modes: letting a sub-category band attach to a named business as that business's revenue
stating a county figure or supplier link without a source, derivation label, or inference flag
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure in any node is a labeled estimate or a cited public fact, no named-business actual revenue or confirmed supplier contract appears, and each high-gross band carries its thin-net caveat with method, source and confidence attached
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a dollar figure
a public-fact source is added or updated
an actual revenue datum (CDTFA, disclosure) becomes available to replace an estimate

nodes.definition: Encode the honesty rule that the 14-business count is a verified floor, not a ceiling — the minimum set of independent Ag & Specialty operators confirmed via public sources (business sites, Yelp/Yellowpages, Turlock Journal), not a claim of completeness. Additional micro-producers (especially cottage-food/farm-stand operators and very small feed/tack shops) plausibly exist below the visibility threshold of public listings and would only raise the count. Source confidence varies by business: Sallaberry, Dairy Solutions Group, Stanislaus Farm Supply, Cipponeri and Ingram's rest on med-confidence aggregator listings (existence and format reliable, finer operational detail not independently verified), while TDR, Lander, Azores, Mid Valley, Cycle Masters, Dale's, Hendrickson's, Turlock Feed and Elite are higher-confidence. Every saturation read inherits the floor caveat so the count is never overstated as exhaustive.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new operator is found or a listing is verified

pros.claim: Reporting the count as a floor prevents the 14 being overstated as a complete census
pros.example: an unlisted micro cottage-food producer would raise, never lower, the count, so 14 is a minimum

cons.claim: A floor caveat weakens any read that needs a precise total operator count
cons.example: a per-capita density read is softer if the true count could be somewhat above 14

failure_modes: stating 14 as a complete count rather than a verified floor
treating med-confidence aggregator listings as fully verified operational detail
acceptance_tests: the count of 14 is stated as a verified floor not a ceiling, the below-threshold micro-producer caveat is given, and the med-vs-high source-confidence split across named businesses is noted
revisit_triggers: a new operator is discovered or confirmed
a med-confidence listing is independently verified or refuted
a public-listing sweep refreshes the catalog

nodes.definition: Render the herd-denominated add/skip verdict for a given Ag sub-category by folding the saturation read, the white-space rank, the growth/decline trajectory, and the licensing/labor/capital gate into one decision. The merged rule: do not add a second bike shop (one-store equilibrium, contracting category) or a fourth music store (already crowded for 73k); the defensible headroom is in the B2B lines (feed, equipment, vet capacity) — each demand-open against the herd base but viable only after clearing its gate (buying-power parity for feed, CSLB trades for equipment, food-animal DVM labor for vet). A demand-true B2B opening that fails its gate is a no-go until the gate clears; a gate-open consumer opening that fails the demand gate is a no-go regardless. Every revenue rationale in the verdict is expressed as a labeled estimate under the honesty guardrail.

included: the gate override on demand-true B2B openings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a saturation, trajectory, or gate input to the verdict changes

pros.claim: Composing all reads into one verdict gives an actionable add/avoid call instead of scattered signals
pros.example: the verdict says no to a second bike shop but yes to feed capacity once buying-power parity is secured

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a sub-category whose demand and gate point opposite ways
cons.example: vet capacity has herd-matched demand yet still needs a food-animal DVM before a clean yes

failure_modes: issuing a yes on B2B demand headroom while ignoring an unmet licensing/labor/capital gate
recommending a consumer addition because the gate is cheap when demand is the binding constraint
acceptance_tests: the verdict for a proposed sub-category combines its saturation read, white-space rank, trajectory, and gate status, refuses any demand-true but gate-locked B2B addition, and refuses any gate-open but demand-locked consumer addition
revisit_triggers: a saturation read, trajectory, or gate feeding the verdict changes
a previously gate-locked opening clears its gate

nodes.definition: Keep the herd-and-acreage market reads from going stale through a refresh loop tied to the agricultural data calendar. A fixed refresh cadence (re-run on each major data release) plus material-change triggers — a new annual Stanislaus County Crop Report (which moves the herd count, ag value and the whole B2B denominator at once), a milk-price or herd shock (e.g., another avian-flu event), a census/ACS or CSU enrollment refresh, a national category release (bike, farm-supply), a CSLB/vet-board/CFO fee or statute change, or a founder-succession event at an aging firm (Sallaberry since 1968, TDR since 1972) — that send the analysis back through DAIRY_ALMOND_BASE, the saturation reads, and the revenue bands. Without this loop the 2026-06-30 snapshot silently goes stale as the dairy economy recovers from its 2024 shock, the bike category contracts, and founder-led firms approach succession horizons.

included: re-entry into the ag base, saturation reads and bands

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

pros.claim: A trigger list with the crop report keeps the lowest-confidence numbers on a path to resolution
pros.example: a new crop report fires the loop and resets the herd denominator behind every B2B saturation read at once

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the reads without new signal, since most inputs update only annually
cons.example: re-sizing the herd base monthly when the crop report lands yearly wastes effort

failure_modes: no cadence set so the snapshot ages silently past its 2024-shock recovery and contraction assumptions
ignoring a fired trigger (new crop report) and continuing on stale herd figures
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and an explicit material-change trigger list exist, each routing back to DAIRY_ALMOND_BASE and the saturation/band reads, with the annual crop report named as the highest-leverage trigger
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs actually update

nodes.definition: Encode the herd-per-practice ratio as an explicit, auditable labeled derivation rather than a stated fact: dairies_per_vet_practice = commercial_dairies / vet_practices = 132 / 3 = 44. This is a derived estimate, not a measured per-practice caseload — it divides the cited ~132-dairy cluster evenly across the three large-animal vets (Azores, Lander, Mid Valley) and ignores per-dairy size variance plus beef, swine and small-ruminant load, so the true working ratio differs. The point of the formula is that the number recomputes transparently from its two cited inputs, so a reader can audit it and re-run it the moment the dairy count changes; it is the canonical worked example of the benchmark-x-size-signal honesty discipline applied to a B2B denominator.

excluded: the broader herd-denominator argument (its own node)
the vet revenue band that uses DVM count not practice count

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the dairy count or vet-practice count changes

pros.claim: An explicit recomputable formula makes the herd ratio auditable and re-runnable on new data
pros.example: when the crop report updates the dairy count, the ratio re-derives transparently from the formula

cons.claim: An even-split formula ignores per-dairy size variance and non-dairy caseload, so the result is directional
cons.example: a few very large dairies could load one practice far above the 44 the even split implies

failure_modes: quoting the 44 as a measured per-practice caseload rather than an even-split derivation
re-using the practice count where the DVM count is the right size signal for revenue
acceptance_tests: the formula dairies_per_vet_practice = 132 / 3 recomputes to 44 from its cited inputs and is labeled estimate-not-actual with the even-split caveat stated
revisit_triggers: the commercial dairy count changes in a new crop report
a vet practice enters or exits
per-dairy size data becomes available to weight the split

nodes.definition: Read why the local advantage is real and where it is not: the dense dairy/almond economy gives the equipment and feed firms short freight, direct-from-OEM dealer agreements and a regional dairy-supply distributor ecosystem, while the vets' cold chain (vaccines, semen) and the equipment firms' wear-parts stocking are operational moats about being on-call and on-hand near the herd, not about price. Cycle Masters bundling free tire changes and maintenance, and the music stores' lesson/rental/repair channels, are the consumer-edge version of the same moat: service-proximity the internet cannot ship. The moat is real for the urgent/fitted/serviced/herd-side dollar and absent for the shippable/price-comparable dollar, which is exactly why that dollar leaks. This node grounds why durable independents here compete on proximity and service, not price.

included: why the moat covers the local dollar but not the shippable dollar

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a proximity, cold-chain, or service-bundling advantage changes

pros.claim: Naming proximity as the moat explains why local independents survive against bigger, cheaper rivals
pros.example: a vet's cold chain and an equipment firm's wear-parts stock keep them on-hand near the herd in a way a distant box store cannot match

cons.claim: Proximity moats protect only the urgent/serviced dollar, leaving the shippable dollar exposed
cons.example: a price-comparable bagged-feed or boxed-bike-part sale still leaks despite the local proximity

failure_modes: treating the proximity moat as a defense for the shippable, price-comparable dollar it does not protect
assuming the moat is about price when it is about on-call/on-hand service
acceptance_tests: the proximity/cold-chain/wear-parts and service-bundling moats are named and tied to the urgent/fitted/serviced/herd-side dollar, with the shippable dollar flagged as outside the moat
revisit_triggers: a national distributor or chain shortens its local delivery/service advantage
a service-bundling or cold-chain capability changes at an operator
leakage of the shippable dollar accelerates

edges.why_related: the dairy/almond base is what gives the Economy A B2B spine its demand, refining the split into its expander
the consumer-edge demand base details the Economy B half of the two-economy split
the herd denominator is derived from the dairy cluster the ag base establishes
the B2B revenue bands are scaled against the county ag base the dairy/almond node sets
the consumer-edge bands (bike, music, cottage-food) are scaled against the resident/student base
the cost/margin pairing attaches to each revenue band so high gross is not read as high net
the band-not-point correction reads off the per-sub-category bands, especially the widest equipment band
the project-mix and DVM-count caveats compound the margin reality in the band-not-point read
the three-gate equilibrium's expander and B2B-cap logic uses the herd denominator
the consumer-cap gate in the equilibrium uses the thin resident/student demand base
the per-sub-category reads decompose the overall three-gate equilibrium into line-by-line verdicts
the consumer-cap gate's leakage component is detailed in the leakage node
the herd-per-practice formula is the worked derivation of the denominator the node argues for
the proximity moat explains the service-and-proximity basis of the competitive structure
the moat covers exactly the local dollar the leakage rule says stays, and is absent for the shippable dollar that leaks
the planting/almond/calving peaks follow directly from the dairy/almond cycle
the back-to-school band-rental and riding-season peaks inherit from the consumer demand base
the trajectory overlay reads the saturated/white-space status of each sub-category before judging growth or decline
the contracting consumer-line trajectory depends on the leakage that pressures it
the demand-open-but-gate-locked premise rests on the herd-matched demand the denominator establishes
the specific CSLB/vet/feed gates attach to the demand-open baseline the premise sets
the inverse competitive map builds on the per-sub-category saturation reads
the crowded/fragile consumer-line competitive read depends on the leakage that exposes it
white-space is the under-served (B2B) end of the per-sub-category saturation reads
durable, demand-open sub-categories rank highest in the gated white-space order
the licensing/labor/capital gate is applied as an override on each ranked B2B opening
demand ranks a B2B opening attractive while the licensing/labor/capital gate can make it un-enterable, pulling opposite ways
edges.resolution_rule: a demand-true B2B opening is a no-go until its gate (buying-power parity for feed, CSLB trades for equipment, food-animal DVM labor for vet) is cleared; demand never overrides an unmet gate

edges.why_related: the guardrail governs how the per-sub-category bands may be expressed and labeled
the guardrail enforces the high-gross/thin-net pairing as part of the honesty discipline
the floor caveat qualifies the counts the saturation reads are built on
the go/no-go verdict consumes the per-sub-category saturation read
the verdict elevates the highest-ranked gated white-space openings as candidate yeses
the verdict applies the licensing/labor/capital gate as the override that turns a demand-true yes into a no
the verdict weighs each sub-category's growth or decline trajectory in the add/avoid call
the verdict must express any revenue rationale as a labeled estimate under the guardrail
the review loop watches the inputs to the verdict and re-triggers it when they change

conflict_axes.name: b2b_demand_headroom_vs_licensing_labor_gate
conflict_axes.description: A B2B line can be demand-open white space against the herd base yet be walled off by licensing, scarce food-animal labor, or capital/wholesale access, so the demand and feasibility views point opposite ways.
poles: block on the unmet licensing/labor/capital gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true B2B opening as a no-go until its gate clears; herd-matched demand never overrides an unmet CSLB/labor/buying-power gate

conflict_axes.name: herd_denominator_vs_resident_denominator
conflict_axes.description: The B2B lines must be read against the county herd/acre base while the consumer lines are read against residents/students; using one denominator for both misreads saturation.
poles: read B2B per herd/acre and consumer per resident
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the herd/acre denominator to the B2B spine and the resident/student denominator to the consumer edge; never mix them

conflict_axes.name: band_point_vs_band_range
conflict_axes.description: Collapsing a wide sub-category band (especially equipment ~$0.5M-$5M+) into a single point figure misrepresents a line whose project mix or DVM count swings it enormously.
poles: use the labeled band with its confidence
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the labeled band is the primary view; the equipment band is the widest and the vet band hinges on an unknown DVM count, so never quote a midpoint

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: A high top-line band (vet, feed) can be mistaken for a high-profit business when the net margin is thin (feed ~2-6%, vet ~10-18%).
poles: read the high gross as profit
pair every band with its thin-net reality
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the revenue band with its labeled COGS/labor/net estimate before any profitability read

conflict_axes.name: dairy_base_expander_vs_correlated_risk
conflict_axes.description: The dairy/almond base expands the B2B count above a generic town but also concentrates risk, since a herd shock compresses vet, feed and equipment demand together.
poles: count rises on the dairy base
count is hostage to correlated dairy/almond risk
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: credit the base for the elevated count but treat the B2B half as correlated, not diversified, risk on dairy/almond cash flow

conflict_axes.name: consumer_gate_open_vs_demand_locked
conflict_axes.description: A bike or music shop is comparatively cheap to open (gate-open) but the thin, leakage-prone household demand is the binding constraint (demand-locked), the mirror image of the B2B lines.
poles: enter on the cheap consumer gate
block on the thin consumer demand
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: for consumer lines the demand gate, not the cost gate, is binding; a gate-open opening with no captive recurring channel is still a no-go

conflict_axes.name: annual_band_vs_seasonal_concentration
conflict_axes.description: A flat annual revenue band averages away the planting/almond/calving/back-to-school/stone-fruit peaks that drive working-capital risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the annual band with the line's seasonal peak profile before any cash-flow read

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous estimate-not-actual labeling protects honesty but can make the analysis read as too hedged to act on.
poles: label every figure as an estimate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure but pair it with a confidence and a confirmation path so the read stays actionable without overclaiming any named-business revenue

conflict_axes.name: coverage_floor_vs_precise_count
conflict_axes.description: Reporting 14 as a floor protects against overstating completeness but softens any read that needs a precise total operator count.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold 14 as a verified floor; let the review loop, not assumption, raise it when a new operator is confirmed

edge_cases.description: A large-animal vet or feed outlet is read as over-built using a per-resident denominator
edge_cases.trigger: a per-10k city-resident benchmark is applied to a herd-scaled B2B line
edge_cases.mitigation: switch to the herd/acre denominator (~132 dairies, thousands of acres) and flag the per-resident framing as inapplicable for B2B lines

edge_cases.description: A sub-category band is attached to a named business as if it were that business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: a per-sub-category estimate is quoted next to a specific operator's name (e.g., TDR, Lander)
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every band sub-category-level and estimate-not-actual; never bind a dollar figure to a named business as fact

edge_cases.description: A high-gross feed or vet band is read as a high-profit business
edge_cases.trigger: a revenue band is used without its cost/margin pairing
edge_cases.mitigation: pair the band with its labeled net margin (feed ~2-6%, vet ~10-18%) and state high-gross-is-not-high-net before any profitability read

edge_cases.description: A demand-true B2B opening (feed/equipment/vet capacity) is recommended without pricing the licensing/labor/capital gate
edge_cases.trigger: a B2B opening is judged on herd-matched demand headroom alone
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the gate (buying-power parity, CSLB C-57/C-61 trades, ~1.3%-food-animal-vet labor) as an override before any B2B yes

edge_cases.description: The 2024 avian-flu quarantine of >110 of 132 dairies is restated as a live 2026 condition
edge_cases.trigger: a year-stamped 2024 herd shock is quoted as current
edge_cases.mitigation: date-stamp the quarantine as a 2024 condition tied to the crop report, not restated as the current 2026 state

edge_cases.description: The B2B spine is treated as diversified risk because it spans vet, feed and equipment
edge_cases.trigger: spreading across the three B2B lines is read as risk diversification
edge_cases.mitigation: classify vet/feed/equipment as correlated, not diversified, risk because all derive from the same dairy/almond cash flow

edge_cases.description: A planting- or stone-fruit-concentrated line is sized on a flat annual band
edge_cases.trigger: an annual revenue band is used for cash-flow planning without the seasonal profile
edge_cases.mitigation: overlay the line's peak profile (planting/almond, calving/irrigation, back-to-school, stone-fruit) on the annual band before any working-capital read

edge_cases.description: A second bike or fourth music store is judged enterable because opening cost is low
edge_cases.trigger: a consumer opening is evaluated on its cheap cost gate while ignoring the binding demand gate
edge_cases.mitigation: for consumer lines treat the thin, leakage-prone demand as the binding constraint; a gate-open opening with no captive recurring channel is a no-go

edge_cases.description: Cottage-Food's whole-business ceiling is set at the CFO cap
edge_cases.trigger: the ~$86,206/$172,411 CFO caps are applied to Cipponeri's entire operation
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the CFO cap only to the processed/dried slice; honey and whole produce fall outside CFO and are demand-/seasonality-limited, not statute-capped

edge_cases.description: A secondary-category straddle inflates a sub-category's apparent saturation count
edge_cases.trigger: a business counted under two categories (Stanislaus FS as feed + equipment) is tallied twice
edge_cases.mitigation: use primary category as the spine and note where secondaries straddle without double-counting the saturation read

edge_cases.description: The count of 14 is stated as a complete census of Turlock Ag & Specialty operators
edge_cases.trigger: an unlisted micro-producer is assumed not to exist because 14 is treated as exhaustive
edge_cases.mitigation: report 14 as a verified floor not a ceiling, noting below-threshold micro cottage-food and small feed/tack shops would only raise it

workflow.action: Split the sector into its two economies
workflow.description: Place each of the 14 businesses in Economy A (B2B spine) or Economy B (consumer edge) and record each economy's demand character
workflow.gate: both economies are named with their three sub-categories each and each economy's demand character is stated

workflow.description: Record the ~$3.15B ag value, ~132-dairy cluster and almond/milk lead as cited public facts and tie them to the B2B count
workflow.gate: the ag value, dairy count and lead crops are cited public facts tied to why the B2B count is as high as it is

workflow.action: Set the herd denominator and consumer base
workflow.description: Derive the ~44-dairies-per-vet ratio and flag the per-resident framing inapplicable for B2B while sizing the consumer edge per resident/student
workflow.gate: the herd/acre denominator is named correct for B2B with the ~44-dairies-per-vet derivation, and the consumer base is sized per resident/student

workflow.description: Derive each of the six bands as benchmark x size signal, tagged estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path
workflow.gate: every band is estimate-not-actual with a size signal, confidence and confirmation path

workflow.action: Pair each band with its cost/margin reality
workflow.description: Attach the labeled COGS/labor/net estimate to each band so high gross is not read as high net
workflow.gate: each band carries a labeled net margin and the high-gross-not-high-net rule is stated

workflow.description: Flag the equipment band as widest/lowest-confidence and name the DVM-count-per-practice as the load-bearing unknown
workflow.gate: the equipment band is labeled widest and the DVM-count unknown is named behind the vet band

workflow.action: Read the saturation equilibrium and per-sub-category ceilings
workflow.description: Set each sub-category count against its correct denominator with a saturated/white-space/capped verdict under the three-gate filter
workflow.gate: each sub-category has a count, the correct denominator read, and a verdict consistent with the three gates

workflow.description: Classify lines as contracting, herd-derivative or statute-capped and attach the herd/harvest/academic peaks, date-stamping 2024 shocks
workflow.gate: bike is named contracting, the B2B spine herd-derivative with 2024 shocks date-stamped, and seasonal peaks flagged

workflow.action: Rank gated white-space and apply the licensing/labor gate
workflow.description: Order the demand-open B2B openings and mark each viable only after its gate clears, with consumer/cottage marked gate-open but demand-/statute-locked
workflow.gate: B2B openings are ranked each with a demand basis and a gate qualifier, and consumer/cottage lines are marked demand- or statute-locked

workflow.description: Combine saturation, white-space, trajectory and gate into an add/avoid call refusing demand-true but gate-locked B2B additions and demand-locked consumer additions
workflow.gate: the verdict refuses any demand-true but gate-locked B2B addition and any gate-open but demand-locked consumer addition

workflow.action: Set the market review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the refresh cadence and material-change triggers routing back to the ag base, saturation reads and bands
workflow.gate: a cadence and a trigger list (annual crop report highest-leverage) routing to DAIRY_ALMOND_BASE and the saturation/band reads exist

priority_rationale: The two-economy split is foundational because every demand, saturation and revenue read depends on placing a business in the herd-scaled B2B spine or the resident-scaled consumer edge; the dairy/almond base and consumer demand base feed the herd denominator and the revenue bands; the bands precede the cost/margin pairing and the band-not-point correction they constrain; the three-gate saturation equilibrium and its per-sub-category reads build on the demand and denominator layers; leakage, competitive structure, seasonality and growth/decline contextualize the saturation reads; the licensing/labor gate (on its demand-open premise) and the gated white-space ranking translate headroom into enterability; the revenue-honesty guardrail and coverage floor govern every figure and count; and the go/no-go verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a decision and a self-correcting refresh keyed to the annual crop report.

dominance_rules.rule: The revenue-honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive number
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named business's revenue or a single market number
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labeled estimate (benchmark x size signal) plus confidence and confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The licensing/labor/capital gate dominates a demand-true B2B white-space opening
dominance_rules.rationale: scarce food-animal labor, CSLB trades and buying-power/capital can make a herd-matched B2B line un-enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a B2B opening is judged attractive on herd-matched demand alone
dominance_rules.action: mark it a no-go until its gate (buying-power parity, CSLB C-57/C-61, food-animal DVM labor) clears

dominance_rules.rule: The herd/acre denominator dominates the per-resident denominator for B2B lines
dominance_rules.rationale: the B2B market is the county herd and acreage, not city residents
dominance_rules.trigger: a B2B saturation read is taken per city resident
dominance_rules.action: switch to the herd/acre denominator and treat the per-resident read as inapplicable

dominance_rules.rule: The cost/margin pairing dominates a high-gross revenue band
dominance_rules.rationale: feed and vet carry thin nets despite large gross, so top-line alone misleads on profit
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-gross band is used to characterize profitability
dominance_rules.action: pair it with its labeled net margin and state high-gross-is-not-high-net

dominance_rules.rule: Correlated-risk framing dominates a diversification read of the B2B spine
dominance_rules.rationale: vet, feed and equipment all derive from the same dairy/almond cash flow
dominance_rules.trigger: spanning the three B2B lines is read as diversified risk
dominance_rules.action: treat the B2B half as correlated risk on dairy/almond cash flow, not diversification

dominance_rules.rule: The seasonal profile dominates the annual band for cash-flow reads
dominance_rules.rationale: a flat annual band hides the planting/almond/back-to-school/stone-fruit peaks that drive working-capital risk
dominance_rules.trigger: an annual band is used for a cash-flow or working-capital decision
dominance_rules.action: overlay the line's seasonal peak profile before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The coverage-floor convention dominates any claim of a complete operator count
dominance_rules.rationale: 14 is the verified minimum, and unlisted micro-producers would only raise it
dominance_rules.trigger: the count of 14 is used as an exhaustive census
dominance_rules.action: report 14 as a verified floor and route any new operator through the review loop

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the vet band (gated by unknown DVM count) or the equipment band carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the confirmation source

dominance_rules.rule: The demand gate dominates the cheap cost gate for consumer-line additions
dominance_rules.rationale: bike and music are cheap to open but bound by thin, leakage-prone demand
dominance_rules.trigger: a consumer addition is justified by its low opening cost
dominance_rules.action: refuse the addition unless a captive recurring channel clears the binding demand gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Place each business in its correct economy before sizing demand, saturation or revenue
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reading a herd-scaled B2B line by a resident denominator and re-doing the saturation analysis

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every dollar figure estimate-not-actual at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read saturation off the correct denominator (herd for B2B, resident for consumer) before counting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a per-resident B2B read that must be re-tallied against the herd base

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair each revenue band with its cost/margin reality when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross band being read as high-profit and requiring a later margin correction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the licensing/labor/capital gate while ranking B2B white-space, not after recommending it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a feed/equipment/vet opening the buying-power, CSLB or labor gate then voids

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the seasonal profile to a line's band when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a flat-band cash-flow plan that must be reworked once the planting/stone-fruit peaks are surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Date-stamp every year-specific ag figure (2024 quarantine, 2020 acreage) the first time it is used
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a year-stamped shock being restated as current and needing later correction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the confirmation path (crop report, CDTFA, DVM-count disclosure) on every low-confidence dollar figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach confirmation sources to numbers already published without them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write each derived ratio (e.g., dairies-per-vet-practice) as an explicit recomputable formula with cited inputs the first time it is used
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a buried magic number that must be re-derived and re-audited when the dairy or practice count changes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new annual Stanislaus County Crop Report lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the ag base and herd denominator and re-scale the B2B saturation reads and revenue bands

iteration_protocol.trigger: a milk-price or herd shock (e.g., another avian-flu event) hits the county
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the B2B trajectory as correlated risk and re-run the affected saturation and go/no-go

iteration_protocol.trigger: a census/ACS demographic or CSU enrollment refresh lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the consumer-edge demand base and re-read the consumer saturation lines

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA sales-tax receipts or operator-level DVM-count/project-mix disclosure becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the affected revenue-band and band-not-point estimates with measured figures

iteration_protocol.trigger: a CSLB, vet-board, DEA or CFO fee or statute changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the licensing/labor gate and re-issue any affected go/no-go verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a national consumer category (bike, music, farm-supply) release updates the trajectory
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the trajectory overlay and re-rank the gated white-space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a sub-category operator enters or exits, or a med-confidence listing is verified
iteration_protocol.action: re-tally the saturation reads and update the coverage floor

iteration_protocol.trigger: a founder-succession event hits an aging firm (Sallaberry since 1968, TDR since 1972)
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the affected B2B line's competitive structure and white-space
